doc.title: Joe Segal — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Roosevelt jazz sessions and Charlie Parker
title: How the Roosevelt sessions were funded
summary: The sessions were volunteer, with a quarter admission rented basses and drums and the money going to the student fund.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Oh yeah. So... very entrepreneurial, which is a testament to your longevity and this music that we love so much. So going back to the jazz club itself, now you’re bringing musicians in, so there’s a financial base there that you know... what do they call it... economic base there, that’s now changed from listening, to now bringing musicians in. You’ve somehow got to pay the musicians...
Oh no, no, no. That was strictly volunteer.
Yeah, we charged a quarter so we could rent the bass and the drums down the street on Wabash Avenue.
And later the guys started bringing their own stuff. We charged a quarter and it went to the student fund.
